name: Al-Yasa (Elisha)
source: Stories of the Prophets — compiled from the Qur'an and authentic hadith
paras: "And Isma'il and Al-Yasa and Yunus and Lut — and all of them We preferred over the worlds." (Al-An'am 6:86). Al-Yasa is honoured in this verse among the chosen prophets.
He was the successor and companion of Ilyas, as Yusha' had been for Musa — the student who served his master, known in the earlier scriptures as Elisha of Abel-Meholah.
When Ilyas, wearied by his people, learned from Allah that a remnant of seven thousand had never bowed to Ba'l, Al-Yasa was of that faithful remnant, chosen to carry the mission after him.

The earlier scriptures tell of his ministry among the Israelites: his counsel to kings, the healing of the waters, and the raising of the dead by Allah's permission — the signs of mercy Allah gave to the family of prophets.

The Qur'an needs no fragment of history to fix his rank: he is named among the best of creation — "and all of them We preferred over the worlds" — a prophet of Israel, a companion of Ilyas, a believing servant of Allah.
Al-Yasa's legacy is the chain of knowledge: the mission passing from a master to his student without breaking — proof that the religion is carried not by blood alone but by sincerity and learning.
